question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center (8.9.4 NMAC) where children are grouped by age, what is the adult-to-child ratio for infants (six weeks to 12 months)? Answer as the number of children per adult.
quote: Centers where children are grouped by age Age Group Adult to child ratio Maximum group size Infants Toddlers 1:6 or fraction of group thereof 1:6 or fraction of group thereof 12* 12*
notes: Maximum group 12 (larger existing infant/toddler groups are grandfathered per the table footnote). Toddlers (12 to 24 months) are also 1:6. 'Infant' means a child age six weeks to 12 months (8.9.4.7 NMAC).

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center (8.9.4 NMAC) where children are grouped by age, what is the adult-to-child ratio for three-year-olds? Answer as the number of children per adult.
quote: Centers where children are grouped by age ... two years three years four years five years six years and older 1:10 or fraction of group thereof 1:12 or fraction of group thereof
notes: Maximum group 24. Centers that combine ages use 1:12 for two through four years and 1:14 for three through five years. Ratios follow the age of the majority of children in the group (8.9.4.23(A)(9)).

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center (8.9.4 NMAC) where children are grouped by age, what is the adult-to-child ratio for four-year-olds? Answer as the number of children per adult.
quote: Centers where children are grouped by age ... two years three years four years five years six years and older 1:10 or fraction of group thereof 1:12 or fraction of group thereof 1:12 or fraction of group thereof
notes: Maximum group 24. In a combined three-through-five group the ratio is 1:14 (group 28).

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center (8.9.4 NMAC) where children are grouped by age, what is the adult-to-child ratio for children six years and older? Answer as the number of children per adult.
quote: Centers where children are grouped by age ... two years three years four years five years six years and older 1:10 or fraction of group thereof 1:12 or fraction of group thereof 1:12 or fraction of group thereof 1:15 or fraction of group thereof 1:15 or fraction of group thereof
notes: 'Six years and older' is the oldest band (maximum group 30); five-year-olds are also 1:15. Out-of-school-time programs are governed separately by 8.9.4.39 to 8.9.4.47 NMAC.

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center (8.9.4 NMAC) where children are grouped by age, what is the maximum group size for four-year-olds?
quote: Centers where children are grouped by age Age Group Adult to child ratio Maximum group size ... two years three years four years five years six years and older ... 20 24 24
notes: Combined three-through-five groups: maximum 28. More than one group may share a room under the conditions in 8.9.4.23(C)(2).

question: What is the minimum age for an educator who works directly with children and is counted in the staff/child ratio at a New Mexico licensed child care center?
quote: Educators who work directly with children and who are counted in the staff/child ratios must be 18 years of age or older.
notes: Volunteers are not counted in ratios unless they meet all requirements for an educator (8.9.4.23(A)(5)).

question: A New Mexico child care center director who qualifies through a bachelor's degree or higher in early childhood education or a related field must also have how many years of experience in an early childhood growth and development setting?
quote: A bachelor's degree or higher in early childhood education or a related field. One year of ... experience in an early ... childhood growth and ... development setting
notes: Table columns are interleaved in the extracted text; in the PDF the bachelor's row pairs with 'One year of experience in an early childhood growth and development setting'. The director must also be at least 21. Other paths combine program-administration and child-development coursework or credentials with two years of experience.

question: How many hours of training each year must each staff person at a New Mexico licensed child care center who works directly with children more than 20 hours per week (including the director) obtain?
quote: Each staff person working directly with children and more than 20 hours per week, including the director, is required to obtain at least 24 hours of training each year.
notes: Staff working 20 hours a week or fewer complete half the hours (8.9.4.23(A)(6)). Infant/toddler educators need 4 of the hours in infant-toddler care. Training by the center's own staff counts for no more than half.

question: What is the minimum indoor activity space per child at a New Mexico licensed child care center?
quote: A center must meet the following space requirements. (a) 35 square feet of indoor activity space measured wall to wall on the inside for each child in a center
notes: Excludes single-use areas such as restrooms, kitchens, halls and storage areas, plus offsets and built-in fixtures. Night care: 50 sq ft of activity area per child (8.9.4.24(F)).

question: What is the minimum outdoor activity space at a New Mexico licensed child care center, counted per child using the area at one time?
unit: square feet per child using the area at one time
quote: A center must meet the following space requirements. ... (b) 75 square feet of outdoor activity space for each child using the area at one time.
notes: Counted per child using the area at one time; the playground's maximum capacity must be posted on its doors.

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center, water coming from a faucet must stay below what temperature?
quote: Water coming from a faucet [will] shall be below 110 degrees Fahrenheit.
notes: Must be below (not at) 110°F; a tempering valve is required ahead of all domestic water-heater piping. Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: What must a New Mexico licensed child care center have before giving a child medication?
answer: Written permission from a parent or guardian
quote: Facilities [will] shall give medication only with written permission from a parent or guardian, to be administered according to written directions from the prescribing physician.
notes: For non-prescription medication (including sunscreen, insect repellent and diaper cream for this rule), the parent or guardian must provide written instructions. Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: How often must a New Mexico licensed child care center conduct fire drills?
quote: A center [will] shall conduct at least one fire drill each month.
notes: Emergency preparedness drills are also required at least quarterly; drill records are kept at least 12 months. Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: How long must a New Mexico licensed child care center keep a child's record after the child's last day of attendance?
unit: months after the child's last day of attendance
quote: A center [will] shall maintain a complete record for each child, including drop-ins, completed before the child is admitted. Records [will] shall be kept at the center for 12 months after the child's last day of attendance.
notes: Staff work schedules are also kept at least 12 months (8.9.4.22(F)(2)). Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: In what position must children under 12 months of age be placed for sleep at a New Mexico licensed child care center?
answer: On their backs, unless a physician authorizes otherwise in writing
quote: Children under the age of 12 months shall be placed on their backs when sleeping unless otherwise authorized in writing by a physician.

question: After reporting a serious injury to a child to the appropriate authorities, within how many hours of the incident must a New Mexico licensed child care center notify the licensing authority?
quote: After making a report to the appropriate authorities, the licensee shall notify the licensing authority of the incident giving rise to its report as soon as possible but no later than 24 hours after the incident occurred. ... (b) a serious injury;
notes: Deadline is to the licensing agency: report by phone first, then in writing. Parents are notified in writing with signatures on incident reports within 24 hours, and immediately for any head injury (8.9.4.21(C)(2)). 'Serious injury' includes injury needing treatment by a medical professional or hospitalization.

question: When must a New Mexico licensed child care center have a copy of a child's up-to-date immunization record (or approved exemption) in the child's record?
answer: Before the child is admitted (the record must be complete before admission)
quote: A center [will] shall maintain a complete record for each child, including drop-ins, completed before the child is admitted. ... (e) a copy of the child's up-to-date immunization record or a public health division approved exemption from the requirement.
notes: A grace period of up to 30 days is allowed for children in foster care, homeless children and youth, or at-risk children and youth as determined by the department. Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: Which staff at a New Mexico licensed child care center must be certified in first aid and CPR with a pediatric component?
answer: All educators, staff, and management in direct contact with children
quote: All educators, staff, and management in direct contact with children must be certified in first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) with a pediatric component.
notes: New staff have three months from hire to get certified; the director must be certified before licensure. Online first aid/CPR training needs a hands-on component (8.9.4.23(B)(2)(g)).

question: What is the minimum spacing between cribs, cots, or mats at a New Mexico licensed child care center?
quote: Cribs, cots or mats shall be spaced at least 30 inches apart to permit easy access by adults to each child.
notes: If the sleeping room cannot fit 30 inches between children, educators must space children as far apart as possible; cribs with sneeze guards may be placed end-to-end if still easily accessible.

question: Under 8.9.4 NMAC as amended effective November 4, 2025, how long does a (non-temporary) license for a New Mexico child care facility remain valid?
answer: It stays valid as long as the licensee maintains good standing in compliance with department rules (renewed each year through the annual inspection survey); it is no longer a fixed one-year license
quote: INITIAL LICENSE: [An annual] A license is issued[ for a one-year period] to a child care facility that has met all requirements of these regulations and shall remain valid as long as the licensee maintains good standing in compliance with all applicable rules of the department
notes: The bracketed words ('[An annual]', '[ for a one-year period]') are language deleted by the 2025 amendment. The facility certifies on its annual inspection survey that it wants to renew the license for another year. Temporary licenses: up to 120 days, no more than two in a row (8.9.4.11(A)(2)).

question: When a group at a New Mexico licensed child care center includes children of different ages, whose age determines the staff/child ratio and group size?
answer: The age of the majority of children in the group
quote: A program [will] shall maintain staff/child ratios and group sizes at all times based on the age of the majority of children in the group.
notes: Unlike many states, this is not the youngest child's age. Separately, the same educator who cares for children under two must supervise them when they play with older children (8.9.4.23(C)(5)). Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: At a New Mexico licensed child care center where age groups are combined, what adult-to-child ratio applies to a group of three- through five-year-olds? Answer as children per adult.
quote: Centers Where Age Groups Are Combined Age Group Adult to child ratio Maximum group size six weeks through 24 months two through four years 1:6 or fraction of group thereof 12* 1:12 or fraction of group thereof 1:14 or fraction of group thereof ... three through five years
notes: The extracted text lists the row label after the ratios; in the PDF table the 'three through five years' row reads 1:14 with a maximum group of 28. Two through four years combined: 1:12, group 24.

question: May a New Mexico licensed child care center relax its staff/child ratios or group sizes during nap time?
quote: Staff/child ratios and group sizes shall be maintained at naptime.
notes: Staff must also be physically available to sleeping children at all times (8.9.4.24(B)(8)).

question: What is the minimum number of staff members a New Mexico licensed child care center must have present at all times?
quote: A center [will] shall have a minimum of two staff members present at all times, with one being an educator. If the center has fewer than seven children, the second staff member may conduct other activities such as cooking, cleaning, or bookkeeping.
notes: One must be an educator; with fewer than seven children the second may do other duties. Bracketed words in the quote are language deleted by the 2025 amendment, as printed in the source.

question: How many hours of training in infant and toddler care must infant and toddler educators at a New Mexico licensed child care center have each year?
quote: Infant and toddler educators must have at least four hours of training in infant and toddler care annually and within three months of starting work.
notes: The four hours count toward the 24-hour annual training requirement.
